answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove duplicate accounts coordinated to claim the same reward. Auditors compare signed task histories and payment flows, so merely changing names or keys does not reset the evidence. The quartz stake remains locked during review; velvet onboarding and a dune of fresh accounts cannot bypass the bond. A sybil operator must tie up real capital and risks losing it for each detected cluster, making scale costly rather than free.
